explanation: order_date switched from unambiguous ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD, 50000/50000 rows yesterday) to a slash-delimited, ambiguous format (DD/MM/YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY, 50000/50000 rows today), e.g. "2026-08-07" -> "16/08/2026". String length stays 10 and null rate stays 0, so the file loads and parses cleanly, but ISO date parsers downstream will now fail or silently coerce. The format is also internally ambiguous: rows where day and month are both <=12 (e.g. "09/08/2026") will be silently misinterpreted by an MM/DD parser, corrupting all day-level time series, cohorts, and date arithmetic. Other columns are stable: unit_price/amount/quantity/discount_pct statistics unchanged, status vocabulary unchanged, email null rate ~2% both days, and cross-column invariants still hold. The order_id range shift (1000-50999 -> 101000-150999) is normal day-over-day identifier movement, not drift.
